description: Out tool is an advanced environmental intelligence application designed to help people adapt, survive, and thrive in any location—from dense urban centers to remote wilderness. By combining real-time satellite imagery, IoT sensor data, and predictive spatial AI, the app analyzes four fundamental layers of the surroundings: surface terrain, groundwater & hydrology, wind microclimates, and nearby infrastructure.
summary:
PolyGeo is a browser-based tool that helps people decide where to build. The user selects any area on Earth, and PolyGeo uses NASA open data to show its geographic factors and key data in one place. It then evaluates the location and gives a suitability verdict for the type of building or structure the user has in mind.

Our standout feature is Sherlock Holmes Mode. Instead of starting from a place, the user starts from their needs: PolyGeo asks a few short questions about the project, then deduces and recommends the best location, like a detective reading clues.

This addresses Be An Earth System Trend Detective by turning complex NASA data into a clear, actionable decision that anyone can use without GIS expertise. Choosing a building site is often guesswork because the data is scattered and hard to interpret. PolyGeo makes NASA’s open, global data accessible to planners, builders, students and communities, helping them reduce risk, save time and make evidence-based decisions about where to build. Better siting decisions mean safer, more sustainable and more cost-effective construction. Everything runs in the browser, so no installation or special software is needed.
details:
What it does and how it works? PolyGeo is a web tool that helps people decide where to build. The user selects any area or place on Earth, and PolyGeo shows its geographic factors and key data using NASA open data, including NASA POWER. The user also says what they want to build, and PolyGeo evaluates the location and returns a suitability verdict for that type of structure. By man-made formulaes.

Sherlock Holmes Mode - our signature feature reverses the usual workflow. Instead of starting from a place, the user starts from their needs. PolyGeo asks a few short questions about the project, then deduces and recommends the best location, like a detective reading clues. And then, gives a PDF-file report

Benefits. All the geographic factors for a site are gathered in one place and turned into a clear verdict instead of raw data tables. No GIS expertise is needed, which saves time and reduces guesswork when choosing a site.

Intended impact. We want planners, builders, students and communities to make evidence-based decisions about where to build, leading to safer, more sustainable and more cost-effective construction, and to make NASA’s open data useful for people who are not data experts.

Tools and technology. PolyGeo is a browser-based web app hosted on GitHub Pages, so it needs no installation or special hardware. Data: NASA POWER, Google maps. Languages and libraries.

Creativity. The Sherlock Holmes theme turns a complex data task into an investigation. Users get questions, clues and a verdict instead of spreadsheets, and the detective approach makes the tool approachable and memorable.

Factors considered: winds, heatm sun position, grounds, and more. We also considered ease of use for non-experts, speed (everything runs in the browser) and transparency, so users can see the data behind each verdict.
